jobs.title: Dynamic PC Support
jobs.description:
The Dynamic PC Support is a position that performs tasks related to the repair of a variety of client products. Performs basic and moderately complex troubleshooting activities for desktops and laptops. May support Desk Side applications and infrastructure. Interacts directly with clients to address technical issues and respond to them timely and accurately.

Responsibilities

• Provide customer support for designated equipment
• Answer client questions in a professional manner
• Accept and deliver all service calls assigned within the established service level agreement for each client
• Meet established customer service satisfaction criteria as outlined in established guidelines and policies
• Complete all administrative tasks associated with each call as documented in established policies and guidelines
• Complete real-time reporting of all calls as documented in established policies and guidelines
• Follow various established policies, guidelines, and documents relating to the successful delivery of service for each client
• Ensure control of assets and inventory through prompt turnaround of parts and equipment as required by client service agreements
• Report all activity in an accurate and timely manner
• Understand all Safety policies and guidelines and work within the guidelines of policies daily
• Additional requirements may exist if offer of employment is extended
• Other duties may be assigned to meet business needs

Education and Experience:

• Typically requires technical school certification or equivalent and 0-2 years of relevant experience
• Previous customer service experience is a plus

Certifications and/or Qualifications:

• Maintain all required OEM Certifications as directed by Management
• Knowledge of relevant software and hardware
• Valid Driver’s License and reliable transportation with valid registration and adequate insurance

Skills:

• Ability to communicate regarding technical issues with clients
• Ability to drive to client locations
• Ability to drive long distances, and occasional overnight assignments within other geographies
• Ability to lift and or move various computer equipment up to 50 lbs
• Must own a basic repair tool kit

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer II
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

We are seeking a highly motivated and talented Technical Support Engineer II to work directly with customers and cross-functional teams on daily support and operational tasks. In this role, you will support Flywire’s Student Financial Services (SFS), eStore, and TPI products for our clients across the U.S. and Canada.

A unique and critical aspect of this role is proactively leveraging AI tools (such as Claude and Gemini) as a smart personal assistant to automate day-to-day TSE workflows, maintain internal repositories, assist with issue investigations, and streamline client communications.

Key Responsibilities:

Technical Support & Troubleshooting

• Ticket Management: Manage and resolve customer and departmental tickets efficiently, ensuring the highest quality standards while strictly adhering to SLA requirements.
• Deep Research: Work hands-on with web-based products and command-line tools to thoroughly research and isolate complex support issues.
• Issue Resolution: Logically assess technical problems, propose accurate solutions to customers, and collaborate with development teams on long-term product enhancements.

Communication & Collaboration

• Client Communication: Communicate clearly, concisely, and confidently with customers via email or phone, translating highly complex technical issues into easy-to-understand explanations based on the client’s technical level.
• Cross-Functional Liaison: Serve as a highly effective mediator and escalation bridge between customers and the product/engineering teams.
• Business Alignment: Align technical support goals with Flywire’s broader business domain, vision, mission, and strategy to deliver on both short- and long-term goals.

AI & Knowledge Management

• AI Repository Maintenance: Manage and maintain the TSE team's AI Skills repository, TSE Project Repos, and internal knowledge base.
• AI Automation: Utilize AI tools to automate routine maintenance tasks, investigate client issues, create bug/product enhancement requests for dev teams, and draft effective, professional client communications.

Here’s What We’re Looking For:

• 3-5 years of experience in technical support engineering.
• 3+ years of hands-on experience with MySQL, Regular Expressions (Regex), and SaaS-based web applications.
• Proficiency in leveraging AI tools - specifically Claude - to optimize day-to-day tasks and boost operational efficiency.
• B.S. degree in a science or engineering field.
• Outstanding verbal and written communication skills.
• Detail-oriented, highly organized multitasker with a strong eagerness to learn new technologies and a drive to go above and beyond to find root causes.

Preferred Qualifications:

• A master's degree in a respective science or engineering field is a plus.
• Experience in higher education, Student Financial Services (SFS), FinTech, or the payments industry.
• Familiarity with industry-standard logging, analytics, and ticketing tooling.

Technologies & Tools We Use:

• Core Technologies: MySQL, Java, SaaS Web Applications, HTTP/SFTP Protocols
• AI Assistants: Claude Code, Google Gemini, Notebook LM
• Operations & Tooling: Zendesk, Jira, Confluence, SumoLogic, Looker

Submit today and get started!

We are excited to get to know you! Throughout our process you can expect to meet different FlyMates including the Hiring Manager and other Flymates. Your Talent Acquisition Partner will walk you through the steps and be your “go-to” person for questions.

jobs.title: Director of IDD Residential Services
jobs.description:
***This position will be overseeing programs within the Lafayette/Kokomo, IN area***

The Director of IDD Residential Services (Area Director) oversees all residential programs and services across the assigned geographic region. You’ll provide leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight to ensure high-quality services for individuals with disabilities while supporting operational growth and developing new business opportunities.

This high-impact leadership role includes oversight of budget management, staffing, licensing, compliance, policy development, program performance, marketing, and proposal preparation. You’ll work closely with Area Managers, Program Directors, support staff, and the state management team to drive operational excellence, strengthen leadership teams, and ensure consistency and compliance across all programs.

This position focuses heavily on leadership development, operational excellence, compliance oversight, financial performance, and strategic growth initiatives to support the long-term success of residential IDD/DD services throughout the region.

WHAT YOU GET TO DO:

• Leadership & Team Development: Lead, mentor, and support Area Managers and Program Directors across assigned residential programs while promoting accountability, collaboration, communication, and operational consistency. Support recruitment, staff development, retention, and leadership growth initiatives across the region.
• Community & Relationship Building: Build positive relationships with families, community partners, referral sources, and external stakeholders while representing Dungarvin throughout the community and supporting regional partnership and growth opportunities.
• Compliance & Operational Oversight: Oversee residential program operations to ensure compliance with state regulations, licensing requirements, Medicaid Waiver standards, HCBS expectations, and organizational policies. Maintain readiness for audits, inspections, operational reviews, and escalated situations across all programs while supporting consistent, person-centered service delivery.
• Financial & Performance Management: Monitor operational performance, staffing trends, budgets, expenses, and program performance across assigned services while partnering with leadership teams to support financial health, operational stability, and long-term program success.

MUST HAVE:

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in human services or a related field required, including Psychology, Counseling, Sociology, Allied Health, or Human Services.
• Experience: 5+ years of experience within residential IDD/DD services, group homes, or community-based programs required.
• Leadership Experience: 2+ years of leadership experience overseeing multiple programs, sites, or leadership teams preferred.
• Program Knowledge: Understanding of person-centered supports, residential operations, Medicaid/CIH/HCBS Waiver services, and compliance standards in accordance to IDOH and CARF.
• Technical Skills: Proficiency with Microsoft Office programs and the ability to adapt to new technology platforms.
• Licensure & Transportation: Valid driver’s license with a driving record that meets agency insurance requirements.

NICE TO HAVE:

• Industry Expertise: Experience supporting multi-site residential IDD/DD programs.
• Regulatory Knowledge: Knowledge of Indiana-specific disability service regulations and HCBS standards.
• Leadership Development: Experience mentoring leaders or supporting operational growth initiatives.
• Operational Insight: Budgeting, financial oversight, or performance management experience.

SKILLS CRITICAL FOR SUCCESS:

• Strategic Leadership & Staff Development: Effectively lead Area Managers, Program Directors, and other operational leaders through coaching, accountability, succession planning, and ongoing professional development.
• Executive Communication & Relationship Building: Clearly communicate organizational priorities, operational expectations, performance concerns, and strategic initiatives while building strong relationships with staff, individuals served, guardians, state agencies, and community partners.
• Problem-Solving & Decision-Making: Evaluate complex operational, staffing, compliance, behavioral, and financial challenges across multiple programs and make timely, well-informed decisions.
• Prioritization & Multi-Site Oversight: Balance competing priorities across multiple locations, leaders, programs, audits, incidents, staffing concerns, and organizational initiatives while maintaining a strong big-picture view.
• Regulatory Compliance & Quality Assurance: Maintain strong knowledge of Medicaid waiver, ICF/IID, licensing, survey, documentation, incident management, and quality standards while ensuring programs remain compliant and survey-ready.
• Workforce Strategy & Leadership: Monitor staffing trends, turnover, overtime, vacancies, leadership performance, and workforce needs while partnering with recruiting and operations to maintain strong, stable teams.
• Person-Centered Leadership: Ensure program decisions, operational strategies, and service delivery remain centered on the rights, goals, preferences, health, safety, and independence of individuals served.
• Financial & Operational Management: Provide oversight of budgets, P&L performance, labor utilization, overtime, revenue, billable services, program expenses, and operational efficiencies while maintaining quality and compliance.
• Change Management & Continuous Improvement: Lead teams through organizational change, identify opportunities to improve systems and processes, and implement sustainable solutions that strengthen program performance.
• Risk Management & Accountability: Identify trends and areas of operational risk, ensure corrective actions are completed, and hold leaders accountable for maintaining safe, compliant, and high-quality programs.

WHY YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE:

You’ll love this role if you enjoy leading leaders, shaping operations, and making a broad impact across multiple IDD/DD residential programs. As an Area Director, you’ll have the opportunity to develop strong leadership teams, drive operational and financial performance, and influence the overall quality of services provided to individuals. This role offers a great mix of strategy, problem-solving, relationship building, and hands-on operational leadership. You’ll play an important part in strengthening programs, supporting growth, and creating sustainable positive outcomes across an entire region.

IMPORTANT INFORMATION:

Dungarvin, Compass, Cambrian are equal opportunity employers.

jobs.title: Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)
jobs.description:
As a Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN), you’ll provide direct patient care in an outpatient setting while working alongside registered nurses, physicians, and other healthcare professionals. Your work will include patient assessment, medication administration, medical record screening, vaccine administration, lab collection assistance, patient education, and support during urgent or emergent situations.

You’ll also help provide health support for trainees and medical coverage for occasional outdoor events while contributing to a collaborative environment focused on safe, responsive care.

Employment Type: Full-Time

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m., including a one-hour unpaid meal period. Occasional weekend work and coverage on some federally recognized holidays are required. A compensatory day will be provided for holidays worked. No services are required on New Year’s Day, Thanksgiving Day, or Christmas Day.

Compensation and Benefits

• Base Pay: $22.40–$24.89 per hour
• Classification: Service Contract Act (SCA)
• Health & Welfare: Up to $5.42 per hour, in accordance with the SCA
• Paid Time Off: 80 hours
• Sick Leave: 56 hours
• Holidays: 11

Key Responsibilities

• Provide direct nursing care to patients with varying healthcare needs, following established clinical policies, procedures, and scope-of-practice standards
• Assess patient needs, complete assigned treatments, and accurately recognize, document, and report relevant clinical information
• Prepare and administer prescribed oral, topical, subcutaneous, intramuscular, and intravenous medications in accordance with established procedures
• Recognize urgent or emergent situations, obtain assistance from an RN or physician, and initiate directed interventions
• Prepare patients and equipment for diagnostic examinations and specialized procedures, assist during testing, and monitor patient condition
• Support trainee healthcare through medical record screenings, EHR documentation, vaccine administration, lab collection assistance, and medical coverage for outdoor events
• Participate in quality-improvement activities, peer review, patient and family education, and the orientation of peers and support personnel

Requirements

• Graduate of an accredited community college, junior college, college, university, or vocational nursing program approved by the appropriate state agency and accredited by the Commission on Nursing Education Accreditation (CNEA); graduate of a State Board of Nursing-approved LPN/LVN training program; or completion of equivalent military training that permits eligibility for the state licensure examination
• Full, current, and unrestricted LPN or LVN license from a U.S. state, territory, commonwealth, or the District of Columbia
• Current Basic Life Support (BLS) for Healthcare Workers certification
• At least 24 months of experience as an LPN within the past 36 months in one or more of the following outpatient settings: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Urgent Care, or Emergency Medicine

jobs.title: Sr Staff Verification Engineer
jobs.description:
Renesas is seeking an experienced Staff Verification Engineer. As mixed-mixed signal verification engineer you will be responsible for the verification and modeling of mixed-signal Automotive power management devices, including PMICs, switching regulators, and related analog IP. You will work closely with design, systems, validation, and CAD teams to drive successful development, integration, and sign-off of complex mixed-signal power chips.

Key Responsibilities

• Design and architect mixed-signal verification environments, including Real Number Model (RNM) and AMS (Analog Mixed Signal) model integration for PMIC designs

• Develop and implement comprehensive verification plans and strategies for automotive PMIC products, ensuring compliance with automotive safety standards (ISO 26262, AEC-Q200)

• Lead debugging activities for complex analog blocks including switched-mode regulators, Linear Dropout (LDO) regulators, and mixed-signal interfaces

• Set up and optimize Gate-Level Simulation (GLS) flows, correlating with RTL simulation results to identify and resolve discrepancies

• Conduct in-depth RTL and Gate-Level simulations, analyzing timing, power, and functional correctness across process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) corners

• Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams: Design, Application Engineering, ATE (Automatic Test Equipment), and Silicon Validation to ensure seamless verification handoffs

• Troubleshoot and debug complex design issues involving interactions between analog and digital domains using simulation and measurement techniques

• Drive continuous improvement of verification tools, methodologies, and infrastructure, evaluating emerging verification technologies and AI-based solutions

• Create and maintain comprehensive verification documentation, test plans, and coverage metrics

• Renesas is seeking an experienced Staff Verification Engineer. jobs.title: Orthopedic Technician
jobs.location: Fort Walton Beach, FL, United States
jobs.description:
As an Orthopedic Technician, you’ll work alongside physicians and nurses to support orthopedic care within a military healthcare environment. You’ll prepare and apply casts, splints, braces, and other orthopedic devices; assist with procedures and wound care; and help patients understand how to safely use and care for their orthopedic equipment.

Employment Type: Full-time

Schedule: Monday–Friday; nine-hour shifts between 6:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., including a one-hour unpaid meal break. Maximum 40 hours per week.

On-Call Rotation: One week, Monday–Sunday, no more than once every four weeks. Respond by telephone within 10 minutes; if called onsite, arrive within 45 minutes of responding or within 60 minutes of the original call.

Compensation:

• Base pay: $22.92–$25.47 per hour
• Health and welfare benefit: Up to $5.42 per hour, in accordance with the Service Contract Act
• On-call rate: $8.00 per hour
• Callback rate: $27.47 per hour
• Paid leave: 80 hours of PTO, 56 hours of sick leave, and 11 paid holidays

Key Responsibilities:

• Fit and apply casts, splints, braces, crutches, and other orthopedic appliances and soft goods
• Assist physicians and nurses with wound care, aspirations, minor surgical procedures, fracture reductions, dressing changes, and the removal of sutures, casts, and splints
• Educate patients on cast and traction care and the safe use of orthopedic devices, while supporting appropriate education for patients and their families
• Maintain clean, organized, and well-stocked cast and supply areas, including coordinating special equipment and supply needs
• Support clinic information systems and data-collection activities while protecting patient privacy and confidentiality
• Follow established clinical, safety, quality, and emergency-response procedures while remaining current with orthopedic care practices and supplies

Requirements:

• High school diploma or equivalent, with additional training or education related to orthopedic care
• At least one year of related experience in an accredited hospital within the past 24 months, resulting in familiarity with orthopedic hospital or clinic routines and procedures, including orthopedic trauma, pediatrics, hand, foot and ankle, sports, and/or spine care.
• Current national certification through the American Society of Orthopedic Professionals or the National Board for Certification of Orthopedic Technologists
• Current Healthcare Provider BLS certification meeting American Heart Association or American Red Cross guidelines
• Knowledge of patient privacy and advocacy, customer relations, HIPAA, and applicable AAAHC, Joint Commission, and clinical practice standards

jobs.title: People Relations Manager
jobs.description:
WHAT YOU’LL DO

You will lead and drive the People Relations agenda across the market, ensuring compliance, supporting business goals, and creating an outstanding colleague experience. You will act as a strategic partner to leaders while providing expertise in labour relations, employee relations, health and safety, policy implementation, and organisational change.

Your responsibilities include:

• Leading and developing the Market People Relations strategy aligned with the H&M Group Colleague Strategy.
• Coaching and supporting leaders on strategic and operational people matters.
• Managing labour law, industrial relations, union and works council relationships, and collective bargaining negotiations.
• Ensuring compliance with local legislation, policies, and internal governance processes.
• Leading and developing the local People Relations team.
• Driving health, safety, wellbeing, and work environment initiatives together with relevant stakeholders.
• Supporting business transformation and strategic initiatives with People Relations expertise.
• Analysing people data and market trends to identify risks, opportunities, and solutions that support business success.
• Collaborating with Global People Relations teams to implement and adapt policies, frameworks, and guidelines locally.

WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH

You will be part of the People function and work closely with Market Management Teams, People Business Partners, Legal teams, Security teams, Global People Relations, employee representatives, unions, and leaders across the organisation.

WHO YOU ARE

We are looking for people with...

• Qualified lawyer with expertise and professional qualifications in Labour Law, Industrial Relations, or related fields.
• A minimum of 5 years' experience leading and developing teams and extensive experience within People Relations, Employee Relations, Labour Relations, or Human Resources.
• Solid experience working with works councils and trade unions.
• Experience resolving complex employee relations matters.
• Experience working in an international and matrix organisation.
• Proven ability to coach and influence leaders on both strategic and operational people matters.
• Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to build trust and credibility across all levels of the organisation.
• Experience driving people-related strategies, organisational change, and transformation initiatives.
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to leverage data and insights to support decision-making.
• Excellent communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
• Professional proficiency in English. Spanish is required; additional languages are considered an advantage.

And people who are...

• Collaborative and committed to building strong partnerships across teams and functions.
• Strategic thinkers who can balance business priorities, compliance requirements, and the colleague experience.
• Proactive and solution-oriented, with the ability to anticipate risks and identify opportunities.
• Inclusive leaders who believe in people and create an environment where everyone can grow and perform at their best.
• Confident decision-makers who navigate complexity with integrity, resilience, and sound judgement.
• Adaptable and comfortable working in a fast-paced, constantly evolving environment.
• Curious and eager to continuously improve processes, ways of working, and the colleague experience.
• Role models of H&M Group values, leading with openness, collaboration, and a growth mindset.

​WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE ​

At H&M Group, we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. ​

• 25% Staff discount on all our H&M Group brands, both in stores and online (H&M, COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories and ARKET).​
• H&M Incentive Program (HIP) – a global program rewarding long-term dedication.
• Development Opportunities: Access to career growth within the H&M Group, with opportunities both locally and internationally.
• Celebrate your birthday by taking the day off.​
• Access to our Flexible Remuneration Plans.​
• Enjoy access to Benefits at Work, the online shopping benefits club with special discounts for all H&M people.​
• Access to GoFluent, a language learning platform for comprehensive language training catered to your professional needs​.
• Access to private health insurance.

JOIN US​

Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.​

​If you feel your experience, skills, and ambitions are a good match for this role, please apply by submitting your application through the career site and initiate a dialogue with your current manager.

Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here.​

To manage applications for roles with leadership responsibilities, we use an online assessment method. You will need to complete it as part of the application and screening process. Your responses will be scored by an assessment tool that applies to predefined criteria set by H&M Group.

After completing the assessment, you’ll have the opportunity to share feedback and ask questions.

If you experience any difficulties or prefer an alternative assessment method, please contact recruitment_support@hm.com. Choosing an alternative will not impact your application. For more information on how we process your personal data, please see our Privacy Notice.

We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter to your application.​

jobs.title: Area Manager
jobs.description:
The Area Manager oversees multiple residential homes and staff teams within an assigned region, providing leadership, operational oversight, and program support to ensure high-quality, person-centered services and compliance with state, licensing, and Medicaid requirements.

This role focuses on team leadership, staff development, program operations, compliance oversight, and problem-solving. The Area Manager partners with staff, leadership, individuals served, families, and community stakeholders to maintain smooth operations, support employee accountability, and ensure consistent, compliant care across all programs.

The Area Manager also plays a critical role in maintaining operational stability, addressing program concerns, and supporting individuals in making meaningful choices within community-based residential settings.

WHAT YOU GET TO DO:

• Program Leadership & Team Development: Supervise, coach, and support employees across assigned residential programs while promoting accountability, teamwork, professional development, and high-quality service delivery. Support hiring, onboarding, scheduling, training, and ongoing staff development initiatives across assigned programs.
• Program Operations & Compliance: Oversee daily operations of multiple homes and programs to ensure services remain person-centered, compliant, and aligned with organizational standards, policies, licensing requirements, Medicaid Waiver regulations, and certification standards. Maintain readiness for audits, inspections, and licensing reviews.
• Participant & Family Support: Promote individual choice, independence, and person-centered planning while assisting with operational, staffing, participant, and family concerns in a positive and professional manner.
• Operational Performance & On-Call Support: Monitor staffing trends, program performance, operational needs, and fiscal responsibilities in partnership with leadership teams while participating in on-call rotation and responding to emergencies or operational concerns as needed.

MUST HAVE:

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Services or a related field required, including Psychology, Counseling, Sociology, Allied Health, or Human Services.
• Experience: 2–3+ years of experience supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, long-term care, or community-based services, including prior supervisory or management experience within residential or human services settings.
• Program Knowledge: Understanding of person-centered supports, compliance standards, and Medicaid/CIH Waivers or HCBS services preferred.
• Technical Skills: Proficiency with Microsoft Office programs and the ability to adapt to new technology platforms.
• Licensure & Transportation: Valid driver’s license with a driving record that meets agency insurance requirements.

NICE TO HAVE:

• Industry Expertise: Experience supporting multi-site residential or community-based programs.
• Leadership Development: Experience with staff development, training coordination, or leadership mentoring.
• Operational Insight: Data-driven performance management experience.
• Regulatory Knowledge: Knowledge of Indiana-specific disability service regulations, including residential and community-based program standards.

SKILLS CRITICAL FOR SUCCESS:

• Leadership & Staff Development: Effectively lead Program Directors, supervisors and direct care staff through coaching, accountability, and ongoing development.
• Communication: Clearly communicate expectations, policy changes, performance concerns, and operational priorities while building strong relationships with staff, individuals served, guardians, and interdisciplinary teams.
• Problem-Solving & Decision-Making: Quickly assess staffing issues, behavioral concerns, incidents, compliance risks, and operational challenges and determine appropriate next steps.
• Prioritization & Time Management: Balance multiple homes, competing priorities, staffing needs, meetings, audits, incidents, and administrative responsibilities in a fast-paced environment.
• Regulatory Compliance & Attention to Detail: Maintain strong knowledge of Medicaid waiver requirements, licensing standards, documentation expectations, incident reporting, and quality assurance while ensuring programs remain audit ready.
• Staffing & Workforce Management: Monitor scheduling, overtime, vacancies, call-offs, training, and staff performance to maintain appropriate coverage and consistent service delivery.
• Person-Centered Mindset: Ensure services are aligned with each individual’s goals, preferences, rights, ISP/BSP, health needs, and level of independence.
• Financial & Operational Awareness: Understand budgets, overtime, staffing utilization, billable services, program expenses, and operational efficiencies while maintaining quality of care.

WHY YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE:

You’ll love this role if you enjoy leading people, solving problems, and making a real impact in the lives of individuals with IDD/DD. As an Area Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to coach and develop teams, improve program operations, and help ensure individuals receive high-quality, person-centered supports. No two days are exactly the same, so it’s a great fit for someone who likes variety, ownership, and being hands-on. You’ll also play a key role in strengthening programs, supporting staff, and creating positive outcomes across multiple residential settings.

jobs.title: Entry-Level Sustainability Opportunities - New York City - Hiring Event with AECOM
jobs.description:
AECOM is hosting an exclusive, invitation-only hiring event in New York, New York October 15th and 16th.  This is a great opportunity to learn and connect with AECOM for career opportunities starting Spring/Summer 2027.

The event kicks off on Thursday evening with a networking mixer from 6-8 pm, where you can hear from AECOM staff about various projects, career paths, and the company itself. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines.

On Friday, interviews will take place at our New York office. This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities.

As a Sustainability and Climate Consultant, you’ll be expected to:

Sustainability & Decarbonization Advisory

• Support the development of Scope 1, 2, and 3 GHG inventories in alignment with voluntary and regulatory standards (e.g., GHG Protocol).
• Assist in identifying and evaluating decarbonization mechanisms and technologies, including energy efficiency, renewable energy, low-carbon fuels, CCUS, and hydrogen.
• Contribute to sector-specific mitigation strategies (e.g., shore power, fleet electrification).
• Assist in modeling GHG reduction scenarios and setting science-based targets.
• Analyze sustainability data (e.g., utility, waste) to inform strategy and action plans.
• Prioritize emissions reduction actions based on feasibility, cost-benefit, and impact.

Climate Resilience

• Support climate risk assessments and communicate key findings from climate models.
• Evaluate resilience strategies for natural hazard mitigation and adaptation.
• Contribute to resilience planning and prioritization frameworks.

Consulting & Project Delivery

• Conduct research and analysis to support strategy formulation.
• Assist in preparing client deliverables, including reports, memos, and presentations.
• Participate in client meetings and contribute to stakeholder engagement efforts.

Cross-Cutting Support

• Contribute to projects involving strategy, climate risk, and sustainability performance.
• Integrate climate and sustainability considerations into infrastructure and energy projects.
• Stay current on climate disclosure frameworks (e.g., CDP, TCFD, SBTi) and emerging policy trends.
• Support ESG strategy development and performance tracking.

Core Consulting Competencies

All Technical Advisory team members are expected to:

• Adaptable to work fluctuations to meet deliverable needs and occasionally work outside of traditional working hours when needed to support global teams and clients.
• Structure and organize ambiguous problems and information, acting independently to drive progress.
• Create and execute project plans with clear goals and measurable outcomes.
• Use data, logic, and sound reasoning to make informed decisions under pressure.
• Synthesize complex content into clear, actionable insights—both written and verbal.
• Deliver polished work products including presentations, models, and reports.

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Sustainability, Public Policy, or a related field.
• Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.
• Strong analytical and writing skills with attention to detail.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior work experience in management consulting, strategy, finance, or related fields is a plus.
• Experience supporting GHG inventories and climate strategy development.
• Familiarity with ESG frameworks and climate disclosure standards.
• Exposure to infrastructure, energy, or public sector projects.
• Experience in a consulting environment with client-facing responsibilities.
• Interest in broader sustainability topics such as water resources, circular economy, embodied carbon, and environmental justice.
• Portuguese proficiency.

• Relocation assistance is not available.
• Sponsorship is not available.
• As a condition of employment, some roles may require travel and a Valid U.S. Driver's License.
• Offered rates of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work locations. The expected salary range for these roles is between $70,000 to $90,000/yr.

To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

The work environment is representative of those an employee would encounter while performing the essential job functions in a warehouse environment which may include loud noise levels, vibration, hot/cold temperatures, and moving objects or vehicles.

• Support safety policies and procedures within the plant
• Safety accident investigation and reporting
• Maintain a clean and safe plant
• Responsible for meeting shift production goals
• Constantly evaluate productivity and current staff to optimize production efficiency and meet schedules
• Provide continuous feedback in an environment that fosters open communication

• Schedule and conduct shift meetings
• Follow all Company policies and procedures
• Regular attendance is essential

• Professional in all communication
• Must exhibit time management
• Professional, detail oriented, and dependable
• Employee and customer driven

• High school diploma
• Experience in a manufacturing environment

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer - Automation
jobs.description:
Senior Automation Manufacturing Equipment Engineering – Rubber Products Production (Hydraulic Hoses, Conveyor Belt, Air Spring, Drapper Belt, V Belts, Etc) – Automation and general equipment and process technical definition. Critical member of the Manufacturing Engineering BA Team, responsible for elevating excellence for Production Equipment and Standardization, Machinery and Production Design, Investments definition, Cost Saving Projects, Automation, and more, across the IAM organization. This role ensures that we define the best process and support or manufacturing operations to produce high advanced spiraled and flexible steel cord high pressure industrial hoses and other related rubber products in a robust, and cost‑effective manner across multiple manufacturing sites.

Serving as both a regional technical authority and a strategic partner to manufacturing plants, this position leads complex process revamp design and automation concepts, equipment selection and industrialization initiatives and ensures consistent launch readiness and stable production performance. Leveraging deep expertise in overall manufacturing equipment and product–process interactions, capacity and layout planning are part of the scope.

The position is responsible for the technical support and definition of equipment and related manufacturing concepts across multiple Hoses, Conveyor Belt, PTS, Air Spring, PTS plants within IAM, directly influencing the successful project technical alignment, technical specification creation, investment financial analysis support, being under capacity increase or cost reduction support projects and continuous improvement of products representing approximately €300 M in annual revenue.

Location:  ContiTech Fairlawn OH. Relocation within US possible.  No international relocation

Tasks

Automation for Manufacturing Equipment Definition and Selection and Improvement:

• Serve as Business Area technical authority for new technologies investment, since rubber hot preparation, confection, curing, cutting, assembly, finishing equipment, etc, ensuring consistent standards and capability across all sites.
• Serve as core expert during end‑to‑end industrialization of new products from design definition through launch and stable serial production.
• Provide expert guidance on manufacturing equipment technologies, materials, and assembly processes, including escalation and problem‑solving support.
• Define and optimize equipment concepts, Automation, tooling, and layouts to meet safety, quality, cost, scalability, and capability targets.
• Support investment initiatives for capital asset selection to manufacture rubber products. Support plants with the cost saving calculation and investment pay back justification.

• Lead improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
• Support structured problem‑solving using Lean and Six Sigma tools (A3, 8D, DMAIC, SPC, MSA).
• Deploy and govern manufacturing best practices and technical standards to ensure consistency and long‑term equipment robustness, with global teams and under global hose manufacturing standards.
• Seek for newer technologies for hose manufacturing with a market perspective and global new trends. Check also existing CT group technologies as bench marking.

Monitoring and Reporting

• Support ME Leadership with reviewing post‑launch manufacturing performance to ensure stable serial production and compliance with industrialization standards.
• Support ME Leadership with monitoring of KPIs for equipment performance and efficiency and profitability gains.
• Identify and assess industrialization equipment risks and coordinate mitigation actions with plant teams.
• Analyze trends and deviations to prevent recurrence and drive proactive improvement.

Standardization & Trainings

• Drive implementation and adherence to global equipment standards across locations.
• Define, maintain, and deploy technical guidelines and best practices in alignment with sector and plant teams.
• Serve as subject matter expert for CS, PTS, DSS equipment industrialization, providing training, coaching, and technical support to engineers and plant teams.
• Support introduction of new technologies, materials, and processes through proper validation, documentation, and standardization.

HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

• Bachelor's degree: in Mechanical, Mechatronics, Manufacturing, or a related engineering or science fields
• 5+ years of extensive experience in Manufacturing Engineering, with deep expertise in equipment Automation, robotics, vision systems, autonomous material handling equipment, remote control and supervisory system.
• Comprehensive knowledge and experience in rubber and plastic production processes and ramp-up projects.
• Deep expertise in specifying and executing projects in automation, integration and supplier and automation vendors administration.
• 20 – 40 % travel availability
• Proficient in English is mandatory

ADDITIONAL  WAYS TO STAND OUT

• Rubber and General Hose manufacturing, Belts technology, including mining belts, industry V belts, rubber air Spring manufacturability
• Production processes & equipment
• Core manufacturing processes (rubber preparation, extrusion, calendaring, curing, cutting, griding, winding up, confection of conveyor belts and similars, testing, inspection, packing, etc.)
• Product and process industrialization technologies, systems, standards, and infrastructure
• Industrial engineering fundamentals and methods
• Design and product manufacturing test processes
• Technical requirements definition to support purchasing process
• Problem‑solving and decision‑making tools (A3, 8D, DMAIC, SPC, MSA, etc.)
• Quality Core Tools (PFMEA, APQP, MSA, R&R, flowcharting, process control plans)
• Lean production / CBS principles, methods, and tools

jobs.title: Pharmacist
jobs.description:
In this role, you’ll assess, evaluate, manage, and support medication therapies for patients of all ages in outpatient and emergent settings. Your work will span dispensing pharmacy operations, medication guidance for healthcare practitioners, and accountability for prescription and controlled medications.

You’ll also chair the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee, with responsibility for formulary management, and participate in other multidisciplinary committees and administrative projects as assigned.

• Position Title: Pharmacist
• Assignment Location: Onsite in Balad, Iraq; relocation required.
• Work Environment: Work is normally performed in a deployed work environment.
• Coverage: On-call availability required.

Key Responsibilities

• Establish and operate a dispensing pharmacy, including prescription intake and recording, accurate packaging and dispensing, and complete medication records. Collect daily data on prescriptions dispensed and the number of patients receiving prescriptions.
• Counsel patients on proper medication use, possible adverse reactions, and polypharmacy. Provide medication education and prescription recommendations to practitioners, advise on potential interactions, and assist nursing staff with medication reconciliation.
• Develop and manage a formulary appropriate to the population and medical services provided. Manage non-formulary, controlled, and other critical medications, including resuscitation medications and medications unique to pregnant individuals.
• Oversee medication ordering and inventory to maintain required stock levels within established budgets. Manage the cold chain for temperature-controlled pharmaceuticals, including vaccines, and oversee expired medication returns to maximize credit when applicable.
• Maintain accountability and required records for prescription and controlled medications. Participate in required monthly controlled-drug inventory counts, audits, reconciliation, and reporting.
• Ensure regulatory compliance throughout medication procurement, storage, distribution, and use. Review and update departmental policies, inspect medication stock and use outside the pharmacy, and report noncompliance to the Chief Medical Officer, Health Service Manager, and Chief Pharmacist.
• Monitor pharmacy operations, report adverse drug reactions and medication errors, and implement quality improvements and corrective actions. Participate in mass-casualty drills as requested.

Requirements

• Doctor of Pharmacy degree (PharmD), Bachelor of Science in Pharmacy (BS Pharm), or country equivalent.
• Hold and maintain a current pharmacy license and registration from your country of origin, with education and graduation transcripts.
• A minimum of three years of experience as a practicing pharmacist, with at least six months of work in the pharmacist career field within the previous 12 months.
• Fluency in both spoken and written English.

Assignment and Physical Requirements

• Obtain medical clearance and maintain current immunizations.
• Possess a valid passport from your country of record before relocation and maintain a current passport throughout your stay in Balad.
• Be able to sit and stand for prolonged periods. Work may also require bending, stooping, and lifting up to 15 pounds.

jobs.description:
The Safety Specialist is responsible for administering, implementing, and continuously improving the company’s environmental, health, and safety programs to ensure compliance with OSHA and company standards while promoting a culture of safety.

Shift: Friday - Sunday, Flex schedule

Duties and Responsibilities

• Develops and implements safety programs such as lockout/tagout, machine guarding, fire protection, and other OSHA safety compliance programs.
• Advises the Company on safety protocols and procedures to ensure regulatory compliance as mandated by local, state, and federal agencies, including the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
• Maintains OSHA logs and other required regulatory documentation.
• Conducts routine and follow-up safety and hazard inspections.

• Facilitating safety committee meetings (developing agenda, providing subject matter expertise, and ensuring compliance with regulations

• Coordinates and facilitates plant safety committee activities. Promote Safety Awareness through communication, education, and participation in safety initiatives.

• Identifies “toolbox” topics and frequency of training.

• Manages OSHA required safety training and certification programs such as First Aid/CPR, forklift, etc. and maintain recordkeeping accordance with regulations.

• Conducts accident, injury, and near-miss investigations; identifies root causes; recommends corrective actions; and tracks completion of corrective measures.

• Work with the Safety Manager, Safety Director, Risk Management, and Human Resources on work-related injuries and illnesses and workers compensation coordination.

• Works with maintenance to ensure all machines and equipment are operating in a safe and efficient manner.

• Monitor and report key safety performance indicators

• Evaluates, recommends, and administers personal protective equipment (PPE) programs.

• Visitor and Coordinates contractor safety orientation and compliance.

• Performs other duties as assigned.

Leadership

• Ensures accuracy and integrity of all safety inspections, training records, and compliance documentation.

• Holds employees accountable for compliance with established safety procedures.

• Supports a culture which values employee safety and food safety.

• Supports a culture of openness and accountability.

• Sets an example by demonstrating professionalism; encourages and insists positive attitudes and behaviors from team members.

• Encourages employee initiative and innovation while recognizing effort and achievement.

• Creates and cultivates positive working relationships at all levels of the organization.

• Adhere to all company personnel policies.

REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

• Associate degree in occupational safety & health or a related field
• Minimum 2+ years of work experience in workplace environment, health and safety programs.
• Working knowledge of OSHA regulations, policies, programs, PPE, environmental policies (EPA) safety engineering, accident/injury investigation procedures, etc.

Preferred:

• OSHA 30 General Industry Certification
• Trained in AED and First-Aid/CPR
• Forklift Trainer Certification
• Previous food manufacturing experience

• Ability to develop and conduct safety training programs for all team members at all levels of the facility.
• Strong understanding of occupational safety principles, hazard identification, risk assessment and control methods.
• Excellent communication skills to convey complex technical information to cross-functional teams and non-technical stakeholders.
• Skilled in performing safety inspections ensuring compliance with OSHA safety standards.
• Able to communicate technical information to non-technical personnel.
• Able to gather data, compile information, and prepare reports.
• Able to develop, implement, and enforce safety programs and protocols.
• Knowledge of federal, state and local safety regulations, protocols, and/or procedures.
• Ability to react calmly and effectively in emergency situations.
• Skilled in developing safety procedures and protocols.
• Ability to investigate and analyze information and draw conclusions.
• Ability to work effectively with diverse populations.

Family-Centered care of children is the focus of this course, exploring issues of normal childcare as well as health alterations of children from infancy through adolescence. Students participate as members of the multidisciplinary health team to provide health promotion, illness prevention, health restoration and maintenance and rehabilitative care to children and families.

In this role, the clinical instructor:

• Implements the College's philosophy, curriculum, program outcomes, and course objectives through clinical teaching and service to the College, community, health system and profession.
• Assumes responsibility for all autonomous aspects of individual teaching assignments.
• Plans clinical experiences for and provides direct supervision and evaluation of nursing students delivering nursing care to an individual or group of individuals.
• Evaluates and provides documented feedback to student on level of performance based on course objectives.
• Is available for remediation of students as required or needed.
• Orients and maintains current knowledge related to agency/clinical policies, procedures, and expectations with the assistance of the agency/clinical personnel.
• Develops and posts written clinical assignments consistent with student's knowledge base, skill competency and individual learning needs.
• Grades homework, quizzes, tests, lab assignments, clinical paperwork and other written work in a timely manner.
• May teach didactic course content under supervision of course coordinator.
• Keeps course coordinator informed of all student and agency issues and concerns.
• Reports to the dean or assistant dean: a course coordinator will also provide direct oversight.

You are encouraged to explore this opportunity if you have:

• A master's or doctoral degree in Nursing from a regionally accredited college or university.
• An unencumbered professional nursing license in the state of Arkansas.
• At least two years professional experience within last five years in the area of instruction as a registered nurse.
• Teaching or precepting experience is preferred but not required.
• Have genuine passion for nursing, education, and lifelong learning.
• Have exceptional subject matter expertise with excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• Are eager to serve students and colleagues with passion, respect and care.
• Illinois RN License will be required to teach all courses (course assignments prioritized to professors who are currently licensed in Illinois)

Operate with a sense of responsibility and purpose with the desire to enrich colleagues, students and the broader community.

Standing

Walking

For short distances for short durations. Surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food-process areas. The height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

• Workers reach above 72 occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on signs, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

• Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

MACHINES, TOOLS, EQUIPMENT, WORK AIDS

jobs.title: Associate Creative Director Copy (Remote US)
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

Directive is a revenue-first marketing consultancy built to serve B2B SaaS, enterprise technology, industrial, and commerce brands. We don't make things look good for its own sake. We build visual systems that hold up under the pressure of performance channels, complex professional services positioning, and a buying audience that starts with a CMO and ends with a CFO.

We are looking for an Associate Creative Director who will translate Moments that Matter into creative territories, messaging hypotheses, campaign concepts, headlines, CTAs, and copy direction that designers can execute against.  The Associate Creative Director will bring senior-level creative judgment to work that is fast-moving, digital-first, and tied directly to business outcomes. This person will not simply wait for polished briefs or execute one-off design requests. They will help shape the ask, identify stronger creative angles, and translate strategic inputs into assets that feel clear, compelling, and differentiated.  They will represent creative in strategic new-business and portfolio-sales opportunities, help build speculative and portfolio creative, and support Directive’s move toward campaign-style case studies that can drive account growth and new revenue.

This is an individual contributor role — no direct reports — but the work will be high-visibility and the standard will be high.  The ideal candidate is copywriting-led and campaign-minded. They should have enough executive presence to participate in client and leadership conversations, but remain hands-on enough to write copy, review briefs, develop messaging territories, and shape creative direction without needing a fully staffed creative team around them. They should understand performance creative as a system of hypotheses, tests, learnings, and scalable winners—not just brand execution or asset quality.

Success means helping Directive replace deliverable-based requests with campaign briefs grounded in business objectives, buyer insight, test variables, and success metrics. The ACD should raise the quality of creative thinking before work reaches production, improve how Directive communicates to technical and enterprise buyers, and create the foundation for a scalable performance creative practice.


WILL OWN

Campaign Strategy

The ACD owns the idea, message, and creative direction before production begins — and helps prove that better campaign thinking can create better performance, stronger pitches, and more creative revenue.



 - Support new-business and portfolio-sales opportunities with speculative creative, campaign narratives, and stronger creative presence in strategic pitches.

 - Create the foundation for Directive’s strategic creative approach.

 - Primary responsibility is creative direction, campaign concepting, messaging strategy, and performance copy direction.

 - Turns campaign and creative briefs into territories, concepts, hooks, headlines, CTAs, landing-page narrative direction, and message sequencing.

 - Partners with designers by giving them a strong concept and copy direction to execute against.

 - Builds the early proof points, examples, and campaign-style case studies needed to support future creative revenue growth.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

30-day success signal: Internal teams understand why this role exists, what it owns, and how creative requests should start shifting from asset asks to campaign briefs.

 - Audited current creative requests, briefs, production workflows, pitch materials, and performance creative examples.

 - Met with Creative Production, Paid Media, Growth, Sales, Account leadership, and executive stakeholders to understand opportunities.

 - Defined what a “good” campaign brief needs to include before work enters production.

 - Created a first draft of the campaign creative brief template tied to Moments that Matter / Stratos.

 - Identified 2–3 priority use cases where the new model can prove value quickly, such as strategic account pitches, paid social campaigns, ABM campaigns, or portfolio-sales opportunities.

 - Produced at least one example of a stronger campaign territory or messaging direction from an existing work.

90-day success signal: Directive can point to live examples where creative strategy made the work sharper before production began, and stakeholders feel the new process is improving clarity, quality, and pitch readiness.

 - Run several real briefs through a campaign-level creative process: insight, hypothesis, concept, copy direction, production handoff, launch, and learning.

 - Developed creative territories, messaging angles, campaign copy, and testing recommendations for priority initiatives.

 - Supported at least one new-business, strategic account, or portfolio-sales opportunity with speculative or campaign-style creative.

 - Built a working partnership model with production designers so designers are executing against clearer concepts and copy direction.

 - Created early examples of campaign-style case studies or internal proof points.

 - Established a lightweight creative review rhythm focused on concept quality, message clarity, testability, and business relevance.

 - Begun defining the message/proof library and taxonomy needed for learning to compound across campaigns.

 - You have an established creative testing rhythm: hypothesis → variant → data → decision, repeatable without manual oversight.

QUALIFICATIONS

Experience & Portfolio

Creative Expertise

 - 4–6 years of professional creative experience, with a meaningful portion in an agency, professional services, or B2B marketing environment

 - A portfolio that shows range across brand work and performance creative — we need to see both a visual system you built and an ad campaign you designed that drove measurable results

 - Experience developing campaigns from concept through execution.

 - Ability to maintain and evolve brand standards across multiple channels.

Strategic and Business Skills

 - Understanding of creative strategy and storytelling.

 - Ability to translate ICP, positioning, personas, JTBD insights, proof points, objections, and funnel-stage context into creative hypotheses and campaign concepts.

 - Executive presence and confidence presenting creative strategy in new-business, portfolio-sales, client-facing, or leadership settings.

 - Strong understanding of performance creative, testing methodology, message iteration, pipeline influence, and revenue-oriented creative measurement.

 - Ability to partner effectively with production designers, paid media strategists, Account Directors, Growth, and Sales without needing to personally execute design production.

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity and helping shape the brief when the request is not fully formed.

Technical and Industry Knowledge

 - Digital marketing and social media

 - UX/UI design

 - Video and motion graphics

 - Content strategy

 - Creative software such as Adobe Creative Cloud

 - AI-assisted creative tools and emerging technologies

Tools — Required

 - Adobe Creative Suite — Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign (expert level)

 - Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro — proficient; you can produce and deliver without a separate editor

 - Figma — design systems, component libraries, collaborative handoff

 - Familiarity with A/B testing and CRO tools — Optimizely, Unbounce, Crazy Egg, or equivalent

 - Heavy reliance and comfortability with generative AI and a recommended tool-set day 1.

Tools — Preferred

 - Project management tools — Asana, or similar; you will work within an existing PM workflow

 - Familiarity with a marketing analytics stack — GA4, Looker, or similar; you can read a dashboard and extract creative implications independently

WHAT WE OFFER

 - 🏠 We have a set living wage at Directive; The annual base salary range for this position based in the US is $120,000-$130,000 USD. This salary range is an estimate, and the actual salary may vary based on Directive's compensation practices, job related skills, and depth of experience.
   
    

 - 🙏  Medical, dental, vision plans, disability, and life insurance coverage for you and your family that fit your lifestyle
   
   - Including a 100% employer-paid plan for you and a 50% employer contribution for your dependents

 - Benefits to Support the Whole Person:
   
   - 🧠  Mental - Access to certified therapists through Spring Health, membership to Headspace
   
   - 💪  Physical - Physical therapy through Omada, fertility support through Carrott, thousands of Aaptiv virtual workouts, complimentary One Medical membership for primary and virtual care
   
   - 🛫 Time Off - Unlimited PTO (2-week minimum), Paid Company Holidays, Your Birthday Off, End of Year Recharge (Closed December 24 - January 1), Paid Parental Leave
   
   - 💰 Financial - Traditional and Roth 401(k) with a 3% company match
   
   - 🌟  Bonus - Annual bonus based on tenure, which scales in total amount over time
     
     

WORK ENVIRONMENT

Directive is a remote-first company. This role operates 100% virtually from your home office. We collaborate through Zoom and Slack. You will need a reliable setup, high-speed internet, and a professional working environment capable of running Adobe Creative Suite and video production software without interruption.

We accommodate global candidates in markets where Directive has established business operations, including Canada, Mexico, and the UK. Current, permanent work authorization in that country is required. Due to the nature of this role, you must be able to remain stationary for extended periods, operate design and video software on Mac or PC, and observe and interpret written and verbal communication consistently. Reasonable accommodations are available for qualified individuals with disabilities — contact recruiting@directiveconsulting.com.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

At Directive, one of our core values is People First. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture in the digital landscape. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

If you require reasonable accommodations in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to recruiting@directiveconsulting.com.

jobs.title: Flex/Utility Officer - Charlotte, NC
Talent Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
At Chapter 2, we’re not just scaling businesses — we’re designing the future of work.We build scalable talent ecosystems that empower organisations to hire smarter,faster, and with far greater strategic impact than traditional RPO models allow.Through a powerful blend of human insight, data-driven intelligence and technology-first thinking, we help companies globally solve today’s talent challenges and prepare for tomorrow’s opportunities.With a global footprint spanning the UK, South Africa, the US, India and Europe, our team thrives on collaboration, curiosity, and innovation. Our holistic approach combines a dedicated embedded talent, best in breed technology and employer branding into organisations across all sectors.

The Role

Talent Intelligence at Chapter 2 delivers bespoke labour-market research,enterprise TA dashboards and analytics for clients and for the business. We helpclients decide where to build teams, what those teams will cost and how their hiring performs.

As our Talent Intelligence Analyst, you’ll work directly with our Talent Intelligence Lead in London. This is a research role first: sizing talent pools, benchmarking pay,comparing locations and mapping competitors, and making sure every number that leaves the building stands up.It suits someone with a real curiosity about AI: you’ll explore new tools, test what theycan and can’t do, and build the best of them into how we research and analyse. Yourwork goes straight into client deliverables and leadership decisions. You don’t need arecruitment background; we’ll teach you the talent side.

What you’ll be doing

• Turn research briefs into structured, well-sourced datasets: salary benchmarks,talent pool sizing, location comparisons and competitor insight.
• Gather and triangulate market data from platforms such as LinkedIn Talent nsights and Juicebox, public data and company filings, until the figures are defensible.
• Automate the mundane, using Claude Code, Gemini Deep Research, LLM APIs and automation tools to speed up collection, cleaning and analysis.
• Act as the quality gate: reconcile datasets, sense-check findings and flag anything that doesn’t add up before it reaches a client.
• Document our methodologies, source notes and runbooks so our research is repeatable.
• Support dashboards, change requests and trackers across the function, and help turn new requests into clear, well-scoped tasks.
• Keep on top of new AI tools and bring forward the ones worth adopting.

What we’re looking for:

We’re looking for someone with advanced knowledge of data, analytics and AI, and the judgement to put all three to work on real research questions.

You’ll ideally bring:

• A sharp eye for data that doesn’t add up, such as duplicate records, gaps or a salary benchmark that can’t be right, and the discipline to check your own work as closely as anyone else’s.
• A genuine curiosity about AI. You use AI tools daily and know the landscape: what Claude Code is and why it leads the field, when Gemini Deep Research earns its keep, and where LLMs go wrong.
• Research rigour: you know a strong source from a weak one and triangulate before you trust a number.
• Advanced Excel or Google Sheets (modelling, lookups, pivots, data cleaning).
• Clear, client-ready written English, and the confidence to ask questions early.
• An experimental streak: you’re happy to try new LLMs, automation platforms and scraping tools, and you hold anything client-facing to a higher standard.It would be great if you also have:
• SQL, and Python for scripting, scraping or analysis.
• Hands-on experience with LinkedIn Talent Insights, Juicebox or similar talent-data platforms.
• Data visualisation in Fabric/Power BI or Tableau, or custom visualisations built with React and Vite.
• Familiarity with Node.js as the runtime behind web apps and dashboards.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Application Engineer
jobs.description:
Sr. Staff application engineer for position in HiRel product group. Primary responsibilities will include supporting existing analog products as well as new product developments for the space market. Products supported include: Precision Op-amps, Instrumentation Amplifiers, Voltage References, Precision ADCs, Battery Management Systems (BMS), Analog Switches/Multiplexers, Current Sources and Drivers, Isolators, and Serial Interface (i.e. RS-422, CANBUS, I2C). Programming experience with Python, Java, and/or C languages as well as knowledge of Verilog coding with FPGAs a plus. Knowledge of using and troubleshooting PSpice models.

• You will be part of an engineering team responsible for device characterization, datasheet and application note documentation, and customer support.
• Work in a multi-disciplinary New Product Development engineering team to help define, evaluate, characterize, and document new product developments with the goal of bringing products to the marketplace.
• Engage with potential customers in support of FAE or Marketing / Sales visits or conference calls to help refine their application needs into deliverable product features for future product definitions.
• Support customer needs as they implement our products into their hardware systems via email, conference calls, or on-site visits.
• Participate in global industry conventions as a presenter.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The Applications Engineering position will be responsible for three main functions:

Device Characterization (50% of time):

You will work with a very talented team of Engineers to perform various lab tests for the characterization of the different products. Prepare the validation plan and compile validation reports upon complete of bench testing/characterization. It is important to understand how the parts are tested to be able to understand their performance when assisting customers. This knowledge will aid in setting up the customer’s exact configuration for verification and characterization of a customer’s issue.

Documentation (20% of time):

You will utilize FrameMaker for generating and editing Data Sheets and then work with the Technical Documentation to publish them. You will be expected to keep accurate lab notes (software of your choice) and document any test procedures for future reference. As you progress in your learning, you will be expected to generate and publish Technical Briefs, Application Notes, Customers Responses, and possibly Articles.

Customer Support (20% of time):

You will work with marketing and sales to facilitate the design-in of our products as well as provide technical assistance to address customer questions and analyze field returns. You will train Field Application Engineers on products and demonstrations systems to enhance sales channel effectiveness.

New Product Definition (10%)

Work with Marketing, Customer, Design and Product engineering teams to help define new products.

JOB REQUIREMENTS/ QUALIFICATIONS:

Need for candidate is time sensitive and therefore preferred to be a US citizen or have a green card.

Candidate must possess a minimum bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Electrical/Electronic Engineering.

Candidate should be self-motivated and conscientious.

Candidate must have excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Candidate must have good presentation skills.

Candidate should have a good knowledge of analog design and lab troubleshooting skills.

Candidate must understand and follow industry standards of test for ICs.

Required Skills:

7 to 10+ Years in Applications and/or Systems Engineering role in Analog IC Development or Circuit Design Industry.

Proficient with analog and mixed signal designs.

Proficient with electronic bench lab equipment (power supplies, function generators, multi-meters, oscilloscopes).

Experience in Schematic/Layout design tools and switching power supply layout concepts (Altium preferred).

Familiar with Microsoft Office (Excel, Power Point).

Experience writing programming code (i.e. Python) to automate lab bench equipment in GBIP/USB communication a plus.

Experience modeling circuits (SPICE and or IBIS) is desired but not mandatory.

jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Director, Individual Markets Insurance Operations, the Service Leader of Agency and New Business Experience function — setting operational priorities, managing vendor partnerships, driving team effectiveness, and aligning sales strategy with operational execution to deliver pipeline performance. This leader will evolve the team's focus from transaction processing toward exception intelligence, process improvement, and firm experience, continuously improving operational efficiency through smarter processes and technology while elevating the value the team delivers to firms and financial professionals. This position is based in Hartford, CT or Des Moines, IA.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Lead daily new business and agency operations, delivering exception resolution quality, service level attainment, issuance velocity, productivity, and customer outcomes aligned with business objectives and process improvement priorities.

• Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team by setting clear performance expectations, building analytical and exception-handling capability, managing capacity, and fostering accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.

• Establish daily, weekly, and monthly operating rhythms — reviewing exception volumes, automation fallout trends, service levels, quality, workload distribution, aging, and operational risks — and drive timely corrective actions.

• Monitor exception volumes and processing trends, partnering with Domain, Product Owner, and Technology teams to refine workflows so the team can focus its expertise on the cases that most benefit from hands-on attention.

• Partner with Third-Party Administrators (TPAs) and vendor partners to ensure operational execution, service quality, and productivity align with business expectations and firm experience standards.

• Lead resolution of operational issues, firm complaints, complex cases, and escalations, ensuring timely follow-through and positive outcomes for firms and financial professionals.

• Implement operational improvements that strengthen quality, reduce recurring exceptions, improve efficiency, and enhance team capability as the team modernizes its processes and tools.

• Partner with Sales Operations Support to ensure daily operational priorities reflect firm expectations, reduce escalation volume, and reinforce an ownership mindset across the team.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

• 10+ years of experience in insurance, financial services, or new business/agency operations, including 5+ years in a people leadership role.

• Demonstrated experience managing vendor or TPA relationships and driving SLA performance.

• Working knowledge of automation and workflow tools (e.g., Pega), with insurance and regulatory knowledge relevant to new business issuance and agency operations.

• Preferred: experience leading operational transformation from manual/transactional processing toward exception-based, technology-enabled service models.

• Preferred: familiarity with sales operations, distribution, or agency management structures.

• Preferred: industry designations such as FLMI, LOMA, or ACS.

CRITICAL COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS

• People leadership and coaching — builds high-performing, accountable teams and coaches with a growth mindset.

• Data-driven performance management — uses metrics, exception trends, and operating rhythms to run the business and drive corrective action.

• Vendor and TPA management — sets SLA expectations, monitors performance, and holds partners accountable to firm experience standards.

• Sales-Operations alignment — partners with Distribution and Sales Operations to translate firm expectations into operational priorities.

• Cross-pod planning and dependency management — orchestrates work across Domain, Product, and Technology to advance process and automation improvements.

• Insurance and regulatory acumen — brings working knowledge of new business issuance, agency operations, and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Operational transformation mindset — shifts teams from production-based work toward analytical, relationship-based, and exception-focused work.

• Trust-based partnership and communication — removes barriers, addresses issues proactively, and builds credibility across functions.
